preconditions.description: The dimensions n, m, number of levels k, and weight w are within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: len(levels) == k and all(len(row) == m for level in levels for row in level)
preconditions.description: There are exactly k levels, each consisting of n rows with m characters.

preconditions.expression: all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ.' for level in levels for row in level for c in row)
preconditions.description: Each cell in every level contains either a letter (case-sensitive) or a dot.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly k+1 lines: one for the total cost and k lines for the transfer plan.
The first line of output is the integer representing the minimum total traffic.

postconditions.expression: all(len(parts) == 2 and parts[0].isdigit() and parts[1].isdigit() for parts in (line.split() for line in output_lines[1:]))
postconditions.description: Each of the k subsequent lines contains exactly two integers representing a level index and a reference index.
The plan specifies a transfer method for every level from 1 to k exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all((ref == 0) or (ref in seen) for (level, ref) in plan for seen in [set()])
postconditions.description: This clause is logically flawed in isolation; the correct logic is that for any level L transferred at step i with reference R, if R != 0, then R must have been transferred at some step j < i. The output order defines the transfer sequence.

postconditions.expression: total_cost == sum((n * m) if ref == 0 else (diff_cost(levels[level-1], levels[ref-1]) * w) for (level, ref) in plan)
postconditions.description: The total cost equals the sum of costs for each level: n*m if transferred fully (ref=0), or the number of differing cells multiplied by w if transferred as a difference from a previously transferred level.
The calculated total_cost is the minimum possible traffic required to transmit all k levels.
